newsitem.title: INDIA: India 96/97 car sales up 19 pct, output up 16 pct.
newsitem.headline: India 96/97 car sales up 19 pct, output up 16 pct.

text.p: India's car sales grew at a slower rate of 19 percent over the previous year to 411,305 units in 1996/97 (April-March), but were expected to hit 850,000 in the next four years, industry officials said on Thursday.
Car sales in 1996/97 grew to 411,305 units from 345,340 a year earlier, the Association of Indian Automobile Manufacturers (AIAM) said in a statement.
"The growth in sales in 96/97 was about 19 percent compared with 30 percent in the previous year," Shripad Bhat, assistant director of AIAM, told Reuters.
Car production in 1996/97 rose to 404,040 units from 348,240 in the previous year, the statement said.
The growth in car output in 1996/97 was about 16 percent, compared to 32 percent a year earlier, Bhat said.
A slowdown in the economy in the second half of the 1996/97 financial year and the high cost of capital were factors that hampered car sales, he said.
"There is no growth in the medium and upper segment of the market," a spokesman for an automobile firm who asked not to be identified told Reuters.
"In the medium segment there was about one percent growth," R.C. Bhargava, managing director of India's top car maker Maruti Udyog Ltd, told Reuters.
Demand was growing at the cheaper end of the price spectrum while most companies were increasing production capacity for mid-range vehicles, analysts said.
"There are too many players in that (medium) segment," Bhargava said.
In the Indian market, cars priced below 400,000 rupees ($11,200) constitute the economy segment of the market while cars costing between 400,000 and 700,000 rupees belong to the mid-sized segment.
"Given the present growth rate, our forecast is that ultimately by 2001 we should reach sales of 850,000," Bhat said.
The new global firms that have just built factories would begin producing and selling in full swing in the next two to three years, he said.

Many foreign car makers, including South Korea's Daewoo Corp, Germany's Daimler Benz, and U.S. companies General Motors Corp and Ford Motor Co have set up bases in India in collaboration with domestic firms.
Maruti Udyog Ltd, a 50-50 joint venture between the Indian government and Japan's Suzuki Motor, produced 328,848 units in 1996/97 against 268,756 a year ago.
The company sold 330,414 cars in 1996/97, compared with 267,020 in the previous year.
